findings.element: ELA (DE) / ELA (EN) textareas in Meldungen — when the cursor is still in one of them
findings.finding: If the caret is in a message box, that box keeps displaying the dispatcher's old text after the underlying message has been replaced from another control, so the visible German text is not the text that was rendered to audio and will be saved.
findings.user_impact: The dispatcher reads, approves and saves an announcement they have never seen — the loudspeakers get a different text from the one on screen, with a green Aus Bibliothek tick claiming everything is in order.
findings.suggested_fix: Always write the current message text back into both textareas on render, preserving caret position, instead of skipping the write for whichever textarea holds focus.

evidence.action: Generated ELA, clicked into the ELA (DE) box and appended a sentence, then — without clicking away — switched Quelle to Library and picked Kein Halt Standardtext (l2).
evidence.observed: ELA (DE) still showed the old edited text while ELA (EN) had switched to the library text, both state lines read Aus Bibliothek, and the audio line read Audio erzeugt 0:10 — a duration computed from the library text, not from the text on screen. Only after the box lost focus did ELA (DE) jump to the library text.

findings.element: Gespeicherte Meldung picker (Quelle = Library) and Aufnahme picker (Quelle = Voice recording)
findings.finding: Both pickers snap back to bitte waehlen immediately after a selection is applied, while the message boxes assert Aus Bibliothek / Mitschrift der Aufnahme and a ready audio file, so nothing on screen says which library entry or which recording is loaded.
findings.user_impact: The dispatcher cannot tell where the text and the audio about to go out came from, and reading the picker literally (nothing selected) contradicts the green tick next to the message.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the chosen entry selected in the picker and name it in the state line, e.g. Aus Bibliothek · Kein Halt Standardtext.

evidence.action: Set Quelle = Library, picked Aufzug ausser Betrieb (l1), then read the picker value back.
evidence.observed: Both message boxes filled with the lift text and showed Aus Bibliothek, the audio line showed Audio erzeugt 0:12, but the picker displayed bitte waehlen and its value read back as the empty string. The Aufnahme picker behaves identically.

findings.element: Save-summary state line above SPEICHERN, when the message boxes show Ereignis geaendert
findings.finding: The save summary ignores the event-changed condition and reports green Bereit zum Speichern while both message boxes are flagged amber as no longer matching the incident.
findings.user_impact: The last thing the dispatcher reads before pressing SPEICHERN tells them the message is ready, so an announcement describing the wrong incident is broadcast with explicit positive confirmation.
findings.suggested_fix: Make Ereignis geaendert a condition of the save-summary line so the pre-save line reads the same warning as the message boxes.

evidence.action: Generated ELA, rendered audio, listened to it so the save line went green, then changed Typ Erstmeldung to Hauptmeldung so the incident became Notarzteinsatz.
evidence.observed: Both state lines changed to Ereignis geaendert and DAISY regenerated to the Notarzteinsatz text, but the audio line still read Audio erzeugt angehoert and the save line still read Bereit zum Speichern; SPEICHERN produced Meldung gespeichert.

findings.element: Save-summary state line above SPEICHERN (single line, first matching condition wins)
findings.finding: The pre-save summary shows only one problem at a time and prioritises the DAISY length warning over the stale-audio warning, so the more dangerous condition disappears from the screen.
findings.user_impact: A dispatcher who over-runs the DAISY limit loses the only warning that the rendered audio no longer matches the text, and saves believing the truncated display is the sole issue while the old announcement goes to the loudspeakers.
findings.suggested_fix: List every active warning in the save area rather than only the first match, and order them by consequence (audio-does-not-match-text above DAISY truncation).

evidence.action: Rendered and listened to audio, edited the DE text to make the audio stale, then filled DAISY with 175 characters.
evidence.observed: The save line was replaced by the DAISY length warning. The stale-audio warning vanished from the save area even though the audio line still read Audio veraltet; SPEICHERN stayed enabled.

findings.element: ELA GENERIEREN button and the ELA boxes during text generation
findings.finding: Text generation has no busy affordance — the button stays fully enabled and unchanged, with no spinner or progress element, the only signal being grey placeholder text — while the neighbouring AUDIO ERZEUGEN shows a real progress bar and disables its play button.
findings.user_impact: During a real multi-second generation the dispatcher gets no sign the click registered and re-clicks the still-live button, and because each completed generation serves the next of three variants with no way back, the text they were waiting for is silently swapped for a different wording.
findings.suggested_fix: Disable ELA GENERIEREN and show the same progress treatment used for AUDIO ERZEUGEN while generation is running, and expose the variant as steppable so a re-click is recoverable.

evidence.action: Clicked ELA GENERIEREN and inspected the ELA zone 250 ms in; then clicked AUDIO ERZEUGEN and inspected 300 ms in; then clicked ELA GENERIEREN repeatedly.
evidence.observed: During text generation: state line Wird generiert, button disabled false, progress/spinner elements found 0. During audio render: progress bar present 1, ANHOEREN disabled. Repeated clicks cycled through 3 distinct variants with no control to return to a previous one.

gaps: ELA GENERIEREN over manually edited text raises a native confirm, but the state map records no native dialogs — the overwrite-confirmation path and its cancel branch were never exercised, so whether the dispatcher can recover an edited text after a mistaken regenerate is unknown.

Audio playback is simulated (no TTS voice in headless), so it is unverified whether angehoert is set only after the file has actually been heard to the end, and whether pressing ANHOEREN on stale audio plays the old or the new text.

SPEICHERN only raises a toast and leaves the sheet open, so the post-save state is unknown — the dispatcher's only confirmation is a toast that appears identically for a complete message and for an empty one.

Switching Quelle away from Standard was only observed together with a subsequent picker selection; whether the previous generated text, its state line and its audio are supposed to survive the source switch with nothing selected was not exercised as its own step.
